name: Judas the Galilean
whenBasis: The census of Quirinius, which Josephus dates to the thirty-seventh year after Actium, AD 6. See the card on the census problem.
summary: A man who, in Gamaliel's speech to the council, appeared in the days of the census and drew people after him; he too perished, and all his followers were scattered. Gamaliel cites him with Theudas to argue that a movement of human origin will fail on its own.
body: Acts says nothing else about him.

moments.text: In the days of the census

later.text: Josephus says Judas the Galilean, with a Pharisee named Saddok, led resistance to Quirinius's census in AD 6, teaching that paying tax to Rome was slavery and that God alone was their master; he calls this the fourth philosophy, from which the later Zealots grew. Two of Judas's sons were crucified under the governor Tiberius Alexander, ≈AD 46–48.
